newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S KOSTNER LEADS IN DOWNHILL PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ITALY'S KOSTNER LEADS IN DOWNHILL PRACTICE.

text.p: Italy's Isolde Kostner posted the fastest time on Friday to top the board in the final practice run for the women's World Cup downhill on Saturday.
"I thought I had some problems with my line today but I guess it was all right," Kostner said.
Kostner has gone from strength to strength to consolidate her first place in Thursday's practice run over the 2.6 kilometre Fatshas course.
Kostner sped down the sun-bathed piste in one minute 25.72 seconds, 0.15 seconds ahead of second placed German Olympic champion Katja Seizinger.
The Italian put her success down to the similarity between the course and the world championship layout in Sestriere.
"Normally I have difficulties on new courses but I liked this one right from the first inspection," Kostner said.
"I took a later start number to simulate conditions in tomorrow's race which starts later than today's training," she said.
Third quickest was Russia's Warwara Zelenskaja in 1:25.91 followed by France's Regine Cavagnoud in 1:26.02 and Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen in 1:26.22.

Saturday's race, the first women's downhill ever staged at the Swiss resort, will kickoff a busy weekend of racing which also includes a slalom combined on Sunday, as the men will be marching in the opening ceremonies in Sestriere.
